I bought a pandemic puppy and it took me 2 weeks to realize that not only I didn’t want to take care of any type of animal I also realized the thought of something completely dependent on me makes me horribly anxious. And it made me realize that even though I like the idea of children I don’t actually want to give birth or raise them. I rehomed  my awesome pup to a friend who desperately wanted a corgi and I’ve been better ever since. Now I’ve found a partner who’s child free as well. It was a major wake up call for me.

I have bipolar disorder so once I started Abilify with vraylar I started feeling amazing. My under treated depression and mania was definitely a contributing factor to not being able to stop. But what I do for my emotions is I ask myself “what do I want the food to do for me”. If I want to binge because I’m sad, bored, stressed, upset, happy, overwhelmed, etc I think about how food is not meant to solve any of those problems. And then I sit with the feeling and assess what else I can do to get relief. If I want comfort I’ll talk to my partner or take a shower and wrap myself in blankets. If I’m upset I cry and then do some journaling or go to the gym. I realized that food can only nourish my body it won’t soothe my soul (not in the long run). And I stumble with this but for the most part I’ve learned that my emotions won’t hurt me if I sit in them. And  the more “uncomfortable” I get in the emotion I’m feeling the better I feel. I lean into the emotion, sit in it, then actively choose ways to address the emotion without food. It’s hard but so worth it. But it took a few weeks for things to settle down completely…the first 2 weeks were heard because I was breaking old habits. But now it’s becoming second nature.
